outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for a divisional clash in Week 7. He rushed 17 times for 58 yards and caught his lone target for two yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6, also losing a costly fumble in the fourth quarter. The outing marked Henry's first this season without a touchdown, and his 60 scrimmage yards were his lowest output through six games. He will aim to bounce back at home in Week 7 versus a Cincinnati defense that allows 19.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.8: Derrick Henry and the Ravens aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they visit Buffalo in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 45 yards and caught one of two targets for four yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Henry has averaged fewer than 3.5 yards per carry (YPC) in two straight outings, rushing 34 times for 103 yards (3.0 YPC) during that stretch. He'll look to turn things around versus a Bills defense allowing 28.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 29th.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenneth Walker continues to shine as the new focal point of Kansas City's offense. Through his first five games with the team, Walker has piled up eight total touchdowns-six rushing and two receiving-while topping 100 rushing yards in four of those contests. He leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, despite already having had his bye and having played one fewer game than Bijan Robinson and James Cook, the only other two backs with more than 600 yards. Walker will try to deliver a revenge game in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenneth Walker was on the receiving end of a revenge game by the Seahawks' defense in Week 7, getting held to a season-low 36 rushing yards and zero TDs. Last season's Super Bowl MVP is still second in the NFL in rushing yards with 701, just three behind Bijan Robinson, and Walker has played one fewer game thanks to Kansas City's early Week 5 bye. Walker will try to stay on course for the 2026 rushing crown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Monangai has missed back-to-back games with turf toe, and he'll need to get back to practice if he hopes to see the field in a TNF matchup. If he is active, he'll return to a favorable backfield role versus a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Monangai will aim to make a return as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Monangai has missed the last three games with a turf toe injury, but Chicago is not planning to place him on IR. This makes it likely the second-year running back at least has a chance to return in the upcoming away tilt. With two 100-yard rushing games and three touchdowns across the first four games of the season, Monangai is an intriguing option if he returns, even against a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Puka Nacua (hip) could return to action when the Rams face Philadelphia in Week 4. Nacua has missed Los Angeles' past two games due to a hip injury, but there is some hope that he can return against the Eagles. While Nacua has been out, Davante Adams has thrived statistically as the Rams' top wideout. The team's receiving corps as a whole could find success against an Eagles squad that ranks 24th in the NFL through three weeks by giving up an average of 24.0 fantasy points per game to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.5: Puka Nacua appears to be past his early-season injury woes as the Rams prepare to host Buffalo in Week 5. The star wideout missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin issue, but he returned this past Sunday against the Eagles and put up a 9-125-0 receiving line on 12 targets while adding a two-yard rushing touchdown. Nacua logged a 90% percent offensive snap share in the contest, so it doesn't appear that he is going to be inhibited by the injury, at least in terms of playing time, moving forward. The Bills present a good matchup on paper, as they've given up the fourth-most fantasy points (27.8) to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Puka Nacua is coming off a massive performance on Monday Night Football with the Rams' Week 6 clash against the Cardinals on tap. Nacua recorded career-best marks with 17 catches and 24 targets in Week 5 against Buffalo, turning that enormous volume into 138 yards and a touchdown while adding nine yards on two carries. The TD was Nacua's first over three games this season, but he's otherwise been massively productive in averaging 10.3 receptions and 112.3 receiving yards per game. The Cardinals don't figure to offer much resistance, as they've yielded the second-most fantasy points per game (28.0) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Puka Nacua should handle an even bigger role on offense following the news that Davante Adams will miss between six and 10 weeks due to a hamstring injury, so fantasy managers who have rostered Nacua could expect a sizable uptick in both volume and production. Nacua has already compiled 37 receptions for 417 yards and a touchdown through four appearances in 2026, and he's had over 75 receiving yards in every game, so the floor is clearly there. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders looks like an ideal opportunity to deliver one of his best performances of the season, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Puka Nacua will look to move further beyond a calf injury when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Nacua played through the issue Sunday against Las Vegas and tallied eight catches on 10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown while adding 10 yards on two carries. He logged an 85 percent offensive snap share, so he didn't seem to be inhibited by the calf injury. With Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to be sidelined several more games, Nacua should continue to see a lot of balls thrown his way against the Chargers, who have yielded a 68.9% catch rate to wideouts, third-worst in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He corralled five of six targets for 27 yards and his first touchdown of the season in Baltimore's Week 4 win. Andrews has yet to top 50 yards receiving through four outings to date, and that trend could continue if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to play on Sunday Night Football. The veteran tight end will aim to find paydirt for the second straight week against Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (15.9) per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught four of six targets for 28 yards and lost a fumble during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Andrews is averaging a solid six targets through five outings in 2026, but he's yet to top 50 receiving yards, only has one touchdown, and tallies 35.4 yards per contest. He'll look to break out versus a Browns defense that's tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back home to square off against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for four yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Andrews turned in his worst performance of the season on a day the Ravens tallied a meager 252 total yards of offense. Fellow tight end Josh Cuevas, a rookie fifth-round pick in 2026, recorded a 4-44-1 line on five targets, finishing second on the team in yardage while tying for second in receptions and targets. Andrews will look to rebound versus Cincinnati's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.2) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mark Andrews and the Ravens travel to face the Bills in Week 8. He caught three of four targets for 23 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 defeat in Week 7. Andrews was unable to take advantage of game flow, as Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and threw for a career-high 298 yards. Andrews has failed to top 30 receiving yards in five straight outings, making him a tough start in fantasy despite the potential return of Lamar Jackson (ankle).

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deebo Samuel and the 49ers travel to face the Falcons in Week 7. The veteran receiver missed San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6 with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5. Head coach Kyle Shanahan stated they would "hold off" on placing him on injured reserve with the Week 8 bye approaching, so it sounds like Samuel is in jeopardy of missing the road tilt against Atlanta. Expect him to work towards a Week 9 return, as long as he doesn't suffer any sort of setback.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashee Rice wasn't able to get healthy over Kansas City's Week 5 bye, and the wide receiver sat out a Week 6 win over the Chargers due to knee and hamstring issues. His absence didn't significantly affect the offense as Kenneth Walker dominated against the Chargers. In his three full games this season, Rice has produced a 13-190-1 line on 17 targets. If he's able to return in Week 7, he'll have a tough matchup against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashee Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring strain, missing his second straight game in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. Before getting injured in Week 4, Rice had produced an 11-171-0 line on 15 targets over the prior two games. Once he's cleared to return, he should immediately be Patrick Mahomes' top option in the passing game. If Rice does get back in the lineup in Week 8, he'll be facing a Broncos secondary that could once again be without Pat Surtain but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trevor Lawrence profiles as a strong Week 8 fantasy starter as the Jaguars return home to host the Colts following their Week 7 bye. In two previous starts at EverBank Stadium this season, Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes. He has a 14:4 TD:INT through six outings, the last two of which came in London. Back stateside, Lawrence should keep rolling at home against a Colts secondary that has allowed an 11:2 TD:INT and could remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).
outlooksByWeek.4: Kalif Raymond will look to continue his tear as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Raymond remained a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 3 against the Eagles, pulling in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Lion transfer has now garnered five or more targets in each game this season, and eclipsed 80 yards in two of three. He'll face a Jets secondary that's been tougher on WRs this season, allowing a top-five 337 receiving yards to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kalif Raymond will seek to reestablish himself as a consistent option in Chicago's passing game against the Packers in Week 5. After totaling 19 catches for 214 yards and one touchdown across the Bears' first three games of the season, Raymond recorded just two catches for six yards versus the Jets in Week 4 with Tyson Bagent under center. The veteran pass catcher will have Bagent throwing to him once again this Sunday, but he will also face a Green Bay defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kalif Raymond will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has now caught five passes for just 12 yards in the past two weeks. Chicago has had struggles at the quarterback position in this stretch, but the veteran still appears behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR pecking order. Raymond will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to his position this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's passing game in Week 7 against the Patriots. Raymond was unable to capitalize on Caleb Williams' return in Week 6, recording just two catches for 18 yards. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond is now situated behind Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland in the target hierarchy. He'll take on a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kalif Raymond figures to be a depth option once again as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Raymond logged his first catch-less game of the season in Week 7, which only supports the fact that his role has diminished at this point in the year. The veteran pass catcher remains a safe option in the passing game, but he's way behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the wide receiver hierarchy. Seattle has ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendre Miller is likely to remain one of the Saints' top rushers while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is out during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Miller received the second-most carries (six) on New Orleans in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but was largely ineffective, averaging just 1.5 yards per carry. Even if Miller continues splitting work with Alvin Kamara, he likely won't have much fantasy value, as the Saints' offense is averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game. Additionally, Miller is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 307 rushing yards all season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendre Miller is expected to remain a large part of the Saints' rushing attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Miller operated as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, receiving more carries (six) and targets (three) while playing more snaps (13) than Alvin Kamara (three carries and two targets on 12 snaps). While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller appears to have assumed the role as the Saints' top rusher. He could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 21.3 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendre Miller appears to have emerged as the Saints' top running back ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller has taken over as New Orleans' primary rusher, logging 22 touches and 70 total yards in the Week 6 win over the Giants. Additionally, Miller played a season-high 46% of the Saints' offensive snaps, which is partially due to Alvin Kamara's injury in the first half, but still remains a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Miller could struggle in Week 7, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 4.0 yards per carry this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Butker missed a field goal for a second straight game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. A resurgent offense under a healthy Patrick Mahomes has given the veteran kicker a solid floor in terms of PATs, and he's a perfect 10-for-10 to begin the year with at least three in each contest. Butker's two FG misses have also been from 50-plus yards, and he's a perfect 8-for-8 from shorter distances. He may not be able to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Raiders team that's allowed 18.0 points a game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harrison Butker has been more floor than ceiling to begin the season. The Kansas City kicker has kicked at least three extra points in all four games, but he's logged more than one field goal only once, going 7-for-9 over that span with both his misses coming from 50-plus yards. With Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker having the offense operating at a very high level, Butker's mix of opportunities isn't likely to change much. He could be busy in Week 6 against a Chargers team allowing 25.8 points per game, tied for 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harrison Butker missed two kicks in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, but he still came away with one of his more productive games of the season, connecting on three of four field goals and one of two extra points. It was the first time in 2026 that the veteran kicker had failed to convert multiple extra points, but his overall volume has been inconsistent, and through five contests he's gone 10-for-13 on FGs and 14-for-15 on PATs. Butker may not be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 7 against a Seahawks team allowing 20.3 points per game, tied for seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harrison Butker went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, the first time he's missed multiple attempts in a single game since 2018. The veteran kicker has missed five of 16 FG attempts overall this season, including one from inside 50 yards, and he may need to turn things around quickly to prevent KC from beginning a search for his replacement. Butker will try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos team that's allowing 20.1 points a game, seventh in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colby Parkinson will aim to be more productive when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Parkinson led Los Angeles tight ends with 47 offensive snaps in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he caught just one pass for six yards. The Rams had three other tight ends log at least 12 offensive snaps in the contest, so the week-to-week individual production among that group could vary widely throughout the season. The Giants held Dallas' starting tight end, Jake Ferguson, to just two catches for six yards in Week 1, so Los Angeles' tight-end corps could have trouble as a whole.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colby Parkinson is uncertain to be able to play in the Rams' Week 4 clash against the Eagles due to a shoulder injury. Parkinson suffered the injury in Week 3 against Denver and finished the game with no catches on one target. Meanwhile, veteran Tyler Higbee put up a strong 8-62-1 line and could be poised for more opportunities even if Parkinson does end up playing. Philadelphia has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 3.0 fantasy points per game to the position, second-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colby Parkinson didn't play in Week 4 and isn't certain to suit up in Week 5 for the Rams' matchup against Buffalo. Parkinson is dealing with a shoulder and a knee injury, and his practice participation level this week should help determine if he'll be able to suit up against the Bills. Tyler Higbee has had consecutive big games for Los Angeles and could work as the team's top TE even if Parkinson is able to play in Week 5. The Rams' offense often provides opportunities for multiple tight ends to thrive, though Buffalo has given up just 6.3 fantasy points per game to the position so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colby Parkinson may have officially fallen behind Tyler Higbee in Los Angeles' tight-end pecking order heading into a matchup versus the Cardinals in Week 6. Parkinson logged just one catch on two targets for three yards Monday against Buffalo while Higbee went off again with a 5-83-0 receiving line on six targets. The good news for Parkinson is that he was able to suit up following a one-week absence, but he's yet to register more than two catches in a game so far this season. With that in mind, he could struggle to produce in Week 6 despite facing an Arizona defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points per game (13.3) to tight ends through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colby Parkinson operates as the Rams' main blocking tight end, and while he's going to have a few catches here and there, he's behind Tyler Higbee in terms of the pecking order in the passing game. The matchup is favorable against the Raiders, who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, but Parkinson's lack of involvement will limit his upside overall. He has just nine catches for 55 yards and a touchdown in five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colby Parkinson could play a key role for the Rams in Week 8 against the Chargers. With wideout Davante Adams sidelined by a hamstring injury this past Sunday, QB Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times. Parkinson logged six of those looks, turning them into a 5-48-0 line. Adams is expected to be out multiple more weeks, so Parkinson and the Rams' other tight ends should continue to be looked to often. The Chargers rank 10th in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends thanks largely to giving up only one touchdown to the position so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darius Cooper continues to flash his big-play ability for the Eagles. Cooper snagged his fourth touchdown of the season last game versus the Jaguars en route to leading the Eagles in receiving yards. Four of Cooper's seven receptions have gone for touchdowns in 2026. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has also likely boosted the opportunities for Cooper, who has 10 targets in his last two contests alone. This trend could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darius Cooper caught just one pass for nine yards last game for the Eagles. Cooper had just two targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Cooper's upside as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Darius Cooper disappointed for Philadelphia last game despite the Eagles dealing with a multitude of injuries at the wide receiver position. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were sidelined due to injury, but Cooper still only managed just one catch for 17 yards. He was targeted eight times in the contest, though rookie Makai Lemon saw eight targets by contrast. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, the matchup still favors Cooper, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.7: Bam Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in Week 6 against the Rams and made the most of the situation, notching 15 carries for 80 yards and outplaying Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. It remains to be seen whether Love will be an option in the backfield in Week 7, as much of that will depend on whether Love is cleared to play, but he's a player worth keeping close tabs on in the event Love isn't 100 percent ready. The matchup is favorable on paper, as the Broncos have given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing tailbacks this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are set to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in Cincinnati's 35-13 Week 7 victory. Tee Higgins garnered the same number of looks from Joe Burrow, but Chase turned his into six receptions for 148 yards and a score. The good news is that the concussion appears to be behind Chase, and he'll be ready to exploit a Tennessee defense tied for 24th in fantasy points allowed per game (35.8) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeVonta Smith returned to the Eagles lineup with a bang. Smith snagged seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown following a two-game absence from a hamstring issue.
