Even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Smith was targeted a staggering 14 times. As a result, even with McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Smith should have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zay Flowers and the Ravens return home for a divisional showdown against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught six of 11 targets for 66 yards and had one carry for one yard during Baltimore's Week 6 loss. Flowers led Baltimore in receptions, yardage, and targets, with no other player earning more than five looks from Tyler Huntley. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question for a third consecutive week, Huntley is in line for his second start under center. Regardless of who is at QB, Flowers will continue operating as the clear-cut No. 1 option in the passing game versus Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (29.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to halt a two-game losing skid when they visit the Bills in Week 8. He caught eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Flowers led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, recording the Ravens' only touchdown in the loss. There's a good chance Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return from a three-game absence in Week 8, but Flowers has proven to be a fantasy stud this season no matter who's under center. He'll face a Buffalo defense that surrenders 42.3 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, the most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.6: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North showdown in Week 7. He missed a second consecutive game in Week 6, a 13-10 loss to Cleveland, due to an ankle injury sustained in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Jackson could potentially get back on the practice field during Week 7 prep, but Baltimore is still considering their star quarterback day-to-day. If he's unable to suit up for the third straight contest, Tyler Huntley will continue to start under center versus Cincinnati's 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.5) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. After missing the last three contests with an ankle injury, he appears to be headed in the right direction, as head coach Jesse Minter stated Jackson is "in a decent spot" to return to action against Buffalo. His practice participation bears monitoring following his limited activity prior to Baltimore's Week 7 loss. If active, Jackson will aim to snap a two-game losing streak versus a Bills defense allowing 26.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Josh Downs has been outplayed by Keenan Allen since the Colts lost Alec Pierce to a heel injury. After exceeding 70 receiving yards twice through Week 3, Downs has compiled a meager 103 receiving yards over the the past three games combined, topping out at 47 yards in a game over that span. His role as a locked-in starter at WR for the Colts makes Downs a viable Week 7 flex play against the Vikings, though he has now gone nine consecutive games without a TD dating back to last season. Minnesota is allowing 133 yards per game to WRs but has limited the position to three TDs in five games, so Downs looks unlikely to end his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Downs has opened his fourth season in Indianapolis on a seven-game touchdown drought, and he has reached the 50-yard threshold just twice this season, with the last such performance coming in Week 3. It has been Keenan Allen rather than Downs stepping up during the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve. Despite his disappointing production so far, Downs leads the Colts with 46 targets and is a decent flex option for Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that's allowing a league-high 210 receiving yards per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dalton Kincaid hopes to rediscover some early season success with the Bills coming out of a bye week to host the Ravens in Week 8. After snagging 12 of 14 targets for 225 yards in his first two games, Kincaid has not topped 38 yards or scored in his subsequent four outings, despite maintaining a higher snap share than last season. Baltimore is allowing only 39.0 yards per game to opposing tight ends, setting up Kincaid for another quiet week, but the Ravens allowed two touchdowns to the position last week and five overall, potentially helping Kincaid break his scoring drought.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and the Seahawks welcome the Chiefs to town for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He's been on the physically unable to perform (PUP)/reserve list to begin 2026, but Seattle opened his three-week practice window back on Oct. 1. With that being said, Charbonnet will need to be activated by Thursday in order to avoid him being out for the rest of the season. He's expected to join the official roster after practicing in a limited fashion the last couple weeks. However, Charbonnet will likely be eased into the backfield rotation if he is indeed able to make his debut, so it would be wise to wait until after the meeting with Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a chance to return to Seattle's backfield in Week 8 against Chicago. Charbonnet has yet to play since tearing his ACL in January, but he was activated off the reserve/PUP list last week and logged a trio of full practices. Though he ultimately didn't play Sunday against Kansas City, another week of practice could be enough for Charbonnet to make his return Monday against the Bears. Should that happen, he'll face a Chicago defense that has given up five total touchdowns (three rushing, two receiving) to running backs through seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. After a Week 3 breakthrough performance, Sadiq failed to record a catch on four targets in Week 4 and now has 21 or fewer yards in three of his first four games. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. A potential Mason Taylor return would further dampen Sadiq's potential.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenyon Sadiq will need to clear the league's concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. After a breakout Week 3 performance, Sadiq has just two catches for three yards (seven targets) over the last two games. New England struggled against Brock Bowers in Week 5 but had previously not allowed more than 32 yards or a touchdown to opposing tight ends. With Geno Smith not throwing a plethora of passes, Sadiq has minimal fantasy allure. Mason Taylor would elevate if Sadiq sits.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game has ground to a halt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. After spiking in Week 3 with seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, Sadiq has only three catches for 15 yards over the last three weeks while sharing looks with Mason Taylor. Miami is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, and Sadiq remains long on potential, suggesting a dart throw as a bye-week replacement is possible, but the floor is minimal.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game is steadily declining ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. After flashing in Week 3 with 105 yards on seven catches, Sadiq has totaled just four catches for 21 yards over the last four games, while Mason Taylor's stats continue to increase. While the Raiders have allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, it's almost all touchdown-related, surrendering eight in seven games but a low 6.5 yards per target average. With minimal volume, Sadiq's chances of reaching the end zone appear minimal.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Branch has received two targets in each of his last three games, even out-targeting Olamide Zaccheaus over the last two weeks (four to three). Additionally, Branch played a career-high 23% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 4 win over the Saints, suggesting his offensive role may be growing. He's also in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 734 receiving yards to wideouts through four contests this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zachariah Branch will likely play a complimentary role in Atlanta's receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Branch has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching all four of his targets for 25 yards. He appears to have overtaken Olamide Zaccheaus in the wide-receiver room but likely won't have much fantasy value without scoring a touchdown. That being said, Branch could succeed against a Bears defense that's giving up 10.4 yards per target to opposing WRs this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow as the Falcons' face the 49ers in Week 7. Branch has caught all six of his targets over the last three weeks, accumulating 34 receiving yards. He appears to have emerged as Atlanta's No. 3 wideout, as Olamide Zaccheaus hasn't caught a pass since the Week 3 win over the Packers. Regardless, Branch will likely struggle in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has given up just 8.9 yards per completion through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Branch played a career-high 37% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 7 win over the 49ers. Despite this, he logged just two touches for 17 yards and will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. That could be difficult against a strong Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just five receiving touchdowns to WRs all season.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain New Orleans' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Vele has been relatively quiet over the last two weeks, catching seven of 12 targets for 68 yards. Despite this, he's played over 90% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the last two contests, suggesting more fantasy production is coming soon, especially if New Orleans continues throwing the ball at such a high clip (39.2 pass attempts per game -- fourth-most in the NFL). Vele could struggle against a strong Steelers defense in Week 7 though, as they've allowed just 6.1 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Spencer Shrader has emerged as an elite fantasy kicker through five weeks, converting all 12 of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last three games. He's 16-for-16 overall this season, including a perfect 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Indianapolis' offense generated plenty of field-goal opportunities in the first half of last season before falling off a cliff in the second half, so the risk of regression is substantial. However, Shrader has an excellent opportunity to keep rolling in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who have allowed 13 field goals through five games, tied with Pittsburgh for the most in the NFL. Keep starting Shrader if you have him.
outlooksByWeek.7: Spencer Shrader has been one of the few bright spots for the 2-4 Colts, converting all of his league-high 18 field-goal attempts through six weeks, including six from beyond 50 yards. His lone blemish on the season is a missed extra point. Indianapolis could struggle to consistently reach scoring range in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game, but Shrader has been too good recently to bench, and the Colts could find themselves kicking more field goals than PATs once again in this difficult matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made (19) and attempted (21), but he was just 1-for-3 in the Week 7 loss to Minnesota after starting 18-for-18 through six games. The Colts' kicker will attempt to bounce back in Week 8 against the Jaguars, who boast the league's third-stingiest scoring defense, allowing just 17.3 points per game. Shrader has earned some goodwill from fantasy managers with his hot start, but he could find himself back on the waiver wire before long if the misses start to pile up.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers return home to host the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He caught two of four targets for 20 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Freiermuth played 34 offensive snaps to fellow TE Darnell Washington's 36, but the two have been essentially neck-and-neck in playing time through seven outings this season. Freiermuth will aim to stand out versus Cleveland's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (13.9) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. In Coker's three full games this season, he's caught 22 of 31 targets for 301 yards and two touchdowns. With Young averaging 40.2 passing attempts per game, it appears as if Coker will continue to produce at a high level going forward. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay secondary that's allowed five touchdowns to wideouts through six games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jalen Coker (shoulder) is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets if active for Carolina's Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Coker underwhelmed in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of four targets for nine yards, his least productive game since Week 7 of 2025. Coker has been one of the league's best wideouts when healthy this season, averaging 5.8 receptions and 77.5 yards per game in his four full games in 2026. If active for Week 8, he could have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Packers secondary that's allowed 35.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).
outlooksByWeek.6: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He threw for 235 yards (22-for-31) with three TDs and no INTs while rushing once for six yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. That's three straight weeks that the 42-year-old has tossed three scores, and he now has a 10:4 TD:INT through five games this season. Rodgers looks to stay hot versus a stingy Buccaneers defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points allowed to QBs (18.4 per game).
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Saints. He threw for 253 yards (33-for-49) with two TDs and one INT while rushing once for minus-one yard during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime. Rodgers led four straight scoring drives to send the game to OT after the Steelers trailed 16-3 to start the fourth quarter. He now owns an 11:4 TD:INT over his last four outings, and he'll face a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. He completed 19 of 30 pass attempts for 212 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for six yards during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Week 7. The performance snapped Rodgers' four-game multi-touchdown streak, although he was able to avoid making any turnovers. He'll aim to get back on track versus a Cleveland defense he threw for 299 yards and three TDs against during a Week 4 loss.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian McCaffrey has had a nose for the end zone this season and will look to score again when the 49ers face the Commanders in Week 6. McCaffrey produced 83 total yards and a TD this past Sunday in a big win over Seattle, giving him at least one score four straight weeks. While his 16.0 touches per game this year are considerably lower than his 24.3 last season, he's been more efficient on the ground with 4.7 yards per carry (he averaged just 3.9 YPC during the regular season in 2025). With that said, Washington has been stingy against RBs through five weeks, yielding just 3.76 YPC and only two total touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers are on the road for a meeting against the Falcons in Week 7. He rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two TDs while losing a fumble, adding nine catches on 10 targets for 53 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 victory. McCaffrey set season highs in carries, receptions, receiving yards and targets while notching his seventh rushing TD in six games. He'll once again lead the 49ers backfield for their matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 23.3 fantasy points per game (21st) to RBs and just surrendered three rushing TDs to the Bears.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: CeeDee Lamb is said to be dealing with a bruise of his quadriceps, but he is not expected to miss any time for the Cowboys. Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards last game as he was dealing with the issue. That snapped a three-game streak for Lamb of at least 112 yards receiving. He will look to get back on track in Week 6 versus the Packers. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: CeeDee Lamb was targeted a staggering 18 times last game for Dallas. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly had a difficult time. Despite the bevy of looks, Lamb managed just 70 yards on nine catches in the 23-13 loss. Lamb has an absurd 44 targets over his last three contests. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: CeeDee Lamb scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Lamb led the Cowboys receivers in all categories, snagging five passes for 74 yards and the two touchdowns.
