He has found the end zone six times in seven contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite Carolina's offensive struggles in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, McMillan was relatively productive, catching four of six targets for 40 yards. On the season, the second-year pro has nabbed 36 of 54 targets for 511 yards (11th-most in the NFL) and two touchdowns in just six contests. He could find success in Week 8 against a Packers secondary that's given up six receiving touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.
outlooksByWeek.5: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.
outlooksByWeek.6: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain for Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets due to an ankle injury. When healthy, he hasn't logged more than a 37% snap share in any of the last three games and has only two catches on the season. The Jets have not faced a prolific rushing offense through five games but have allowed two opposing backs to gain at least 99 yards. If active, a split role with Rhamondre Stevenson caps Henderson's appeal against a defense allowing a stingy 4.3 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: TreVeyon Henderson figures to handle a modest workload in the Patriots' Week 7 matchup against the Bears. Making a surprise appearance in Week 6 after suffering a high-ankle sprain, Henderson recorded seven carries for 31 yards while also catching his third pass of the season. Rhamondre Stevenson continues to garner a bigger workload but has plodded to a career-low 3.7 yards per carry. Until New England trusts Henderson in pass protection and ball security, however, a change in roles appears unlikely. Facing a Chicago defense on a short turnaround with Week 7's Thursday night kickoff, Henderson will need to solve a run defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to date.
outlooksByWeek.8: TreVeyon Henderson's declining role in the Patriots' rushing approach leads to low expectations in a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. He has logged single-digit carries in three straight games and sits with a 3.9 yards per carry average after a 5.1 mark as a rookie. He's also only caught four passes, an area where Miami has been particularly vulnerable against running backs. With New England seemingly happy to distribute the workload across multiple players, an uptick in usage for Henderson appears unlikely.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference clash in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for nine yards during Cleveland's 13-10 Week 6 win. Following a three-game stretch in which he recorded a 15-132-3 receiving line on 20 targets, Fannin has now gone two straight outings with one reception and fewer than 10 yards. The second-year TE will try to bounce back versus a Titans defense allowing 10.5 fantasy points per game (T-7th) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns visit the Steelers for an AFC North battle in Week 8. He brought in six of nine targets for 91 yards and also lost a fumble during Cleveland's 27-24 Week 7 win. Fannin finished second behind KC Concepcion (8-129-0 on 10 targets) in receptions, yardage, and targets while setting a new season high in receiving yards. Fannin will look to exploit the Pittsburgh defense again after he recorded a 3-27-1 line against them in a Week 4 victory.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashid Shaheed isn't certain to suit up for Seattle in Week 8 against the Bears. Shaheed injured his knee in Week 7 versus Kansas City, and though initial reports on the injury were promising, it's not clear if he'll need to miss time. The versatile wideout has been pretty quiet as a receiver throughout the campaign, surpassing three receptions just once through seven weeks. That makes him relatively dependent on big plays, and Chicago has given up nine receptions of 40-plus yards this season, most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for eight yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Judkins returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury and posted his best performance of the year, setting season highs in rush yards and yards from scrimmage (104). He'll aim to stay hot against a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the Buccaneers' main offensive weapon in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Irving was largely ineffective against the Packers in a Week 4 loss, rushing for 61 yards on 16 carries. Additionally, the Oregon product was held without a target after accumulating 15 in Tampa Bay's first three games, suggesting Irving is likely in for less pass-catching opportunities while Jalon Daniels remains the starting quarterback. Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Irving was phenomenal in the Week 5 upset win over the Cowboys, totaling 175 yards and two touchdowns on 23 touches. Despite this, Irving is seeing less receiving work since Jalon Daniels took over for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback, getting just three targets over his last two games. Even so, Irving should remain productive in Week 6 against a Steelers defense that's allowed 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was relatively quiet in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, totaling 49 yards on 22 touches. Despite this, he remains firmly ahead of Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker in Tampa Bay's backfield and could thrive in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has allowed 25.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season. Additionally, Irving could benefit from the possible return of quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), as Irving averaged 5.0 targets per game while Mayfield was healthy (just 2.0 since Mayfield's injury).
outlooksByWeek.8: Bucky Irving will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Irving carried the load for Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing for 106 and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for four yards. Irving has been the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense over the last three weeks, averaging 111.3 total yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game during that span. He's in for a very favorable Week 8 matchup as well, with Atlanta's defense allowing 26.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.7: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.
outlooksByWeek.8: Adonai Mitchell has a minimal role in the Jets' limited passing attack entering a Week 8 clash with the Raiders. Returning from a four-week absence in Week 7, Mitchell failed to record a catch on his three targets. Omar Cooper's emergence paired with Garrett Wilson's steady presence won't leave a plethora of opportunities for the remaining Jets' receivers in a run-first offense, giving Mitchell too few chances to exploit a defense that's allowing a generous 8.9 yards per target through seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Kirk and the 49ers hope to improve to 7-0 when they visit Atlanta in Week 7. The veteran receiver has been on the reserve/PUP list to begin 2026 due to a calf injury and has yet to suit up for San Francisco. The 49ers opened Kirk's practice window on Oct. 15 and there were reports of him possibly being activated for Week 6, but that was indeed not the case. With Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road clash against the Falcons, San Francisco could really use Kirk's presence on the field.

player.seasonOutlook: Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a bad-weather win over the Bears in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his PATs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13.0) so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,
outlooksByWeek.7: Will Reichard remains a high-volume option once again as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 5 before Minnesota's bye, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts and two XPAs. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last four games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Colts squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to kickers (10.3) this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Will Reichard should remain a high-usage option as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Reichard stayed busy in Week 7 against the Colts, but he did miss his first kick of the season going 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts. Even so, the third-year boot has now gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, and nailed all nine of his XPAs this season. Detroit has ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to kickers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Higbee has emerged as the Rams' most productive receiving tight end, catching 24 passes for 246 yards and a touchdown through six games. Even though he delivered a subpar showing in Week 6 against the Cardinals, finishing with four catches for 22 yards, he's clearly ahead of Colby Parkinson in the pecking order in the passing game. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the time being, Higbee should be one of the players in line for an uptick in targets and touches. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable on paper, as Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Higbee continues to work in an unpredictable Rams tight-end timeshare ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Chargers. While Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Higbee got just three of those looks and put up a meager 2-14-0 line. Meanwhile, fellow TEs Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had bigger performances. Wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss several weeks, so Stafford will likely continue to look to his tight ends often, but it's anyone's guess which of the trio will be the top performer on a week-to-week basis. The Chargers have been relatively stingy against tight ends, giving up 6.8 fantasy points per game, tied for 10th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rome Odunze will look to do more as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Odunze brought in just three of four targets for 39 yards in Week 6, which was a bit of a bummer, with Caleb Williams throwing for 305 yards. The third-year pass catcher has been held in check in more games than not this season, catching 20 of 33 targets for 312 yards with zero touchdowns. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rome Odunze will look to capitalize on his opportunities as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Odunze was outperformed by teammate Luther Burden once again in Week 7 against the Patriots, logging four catches for 69 yards to Burden's four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown. Odunze has still been solid throughout this year, with a 24-381-0 receiving line over the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Seahawks defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omar Cooper's two-week surge is set to extend into Week 8 when the Jets have an inviting matchup with the Raiders. Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored in consecutive outings since returning from an ankle injury, while snagging 11 of his 12 targets. The volume remains modest in a run-first offense, but Las Vegas is allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wide receivers with seven similar players registering at least 53 receiving yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylin Noel continues to make the most of his opportunities for the Texans. The 2025 third-round pick has caught every pass thrown his way in four of five games this season, leads the team with 17.5 yards per catch and just scored his first TD of the campaign while tying his season high with five targets in the Week 5 win over Tennessee. Noel's arrow is pointing up ahead of a Week 6 matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing a league-high 204 receiving yards per game to WRs, though his floor remains low due to modest volume, as he has earned just 17 targets through five games. He's a boom-or-bust Week 6 flex option for managers in deeper leagues or in search of a bye-week plug-in.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylin Noel has made the most of his opportunities all season, and Houston's 2025 third-round pick has started to earn a larger role in recent weeks. He takes a two-game touchdown streak into Week 7 against the Giants. Noel has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over the past three games after posting five catches for 101 yards on nine targets through Week 3. Nico Collins remains the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game, and the role of trade acquisition Marvin Harrison should grow moving forward, but Noel's recent success makes him a viable Week 7 flex play against a Giants secondary that has allowed seven receiving TDs to WRs in six games.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jonathan Taylor has topped 90 rushing yards four times this season and has seven TDs, while the rest of the Colts' offense has scored six touchdowns combined. The star RB remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 for Week 7, even in a difficult matchup with a stout Vikings defense that's allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game (fifth-fewest) and a league-low 12.8 points per game. Opponents have been stacking the box against Taylor with Daniel Jones struggling to make defenses pay through the air, but Taylor has overcome those difficult situations to rank among the league's most productive players at his position as usual, despite the lack of help from his teammates.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonathan Taylor has at least 92 rushing yards and a TD in five of the Colts' seven games, keeping him firmly in set-and-forget fantasy RB1 territory for Week 8 despite a difficult matchup against Jacksonville's elite front. The Jaguars are allowing a league-low 72 rushing yards per game and boast the league's third-best scoring defense at 17.3 points per game. Taylor has handled 20-plus touches in all but one game this season and should remain busy in Week 8, as long as the 2-5 Colts stay within striking distance of the 4-2 Jaguars.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024.
