outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.
outlooksByWeek.5: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.
outlooksByWeek.7: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.
outlooksByWeek.8: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 showdown with first place in the AFC North on the line. He brought in two of six targets for 56 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Paris. Metcalf tied for the lead in targets while pacing the team in yardage despite his low reception count. He'll be ready to face a Cleveland defense he cooked for a season-high 115 yards on five catches in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards last game for the Eagles. Goedert was second on the team in targets behind DeVonta Smith. Even with Tanner McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Goedert should still have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dallas Goedert finished second on the Eagles last game in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Goedert caught five passes on seven looks for 48 yards in the 38-21 loss to the Cowboys. Goedert has at least seven targets in three-straight outings. If DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Goedert should remain a focal point of the passing attack, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyjae Spears was limited to three touches for the Titans in Week 3 while playing through an ankle injury. Even if he heals up ahead of a Week 4 trip to Baltimore, Spears is unlikely to crack double-digits in touches while filling his customary change-of-pace role behind Tony Pollard. The Ravens have been middling against the run but have limited RBs to just 12 receiving yards per game, so Spears is unlikely to earn much Week 4 fantasy lineup consideration outside of super-deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyjae Spears has been limited to three touches in each of Tennessee's Week 3 and Week 4 games while playing through an ankle injury. Typically, his total is in the high single digits, but Spears' injury concerns, coupled with Tennessee's struggles on offense (13.8 points per game), make the change-of-pace RB a fantasy non-factor ahead of a Week 5 home game against the Texans, who are allowing just 3.5 yards per carry. Tony Pollard should continue to get the majority of opportunities in Tennessee's backfield.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyjae Spears had a season-high 11 touches, including nine catches, in Tennessee's Week 5 loss to the Texans. His contributions as a receiver give Spears some deep-league flex appeal for Week 6 against a Colts defense that's allowing a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to running backs. Tony Pollard remains the top backfield option in a low-octane Titans offense that's scoring a league-low 11.6 points per game, while Spears has only one game with more than 28 scrimmage yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyjae Spears exceeded three touches in only one of the Titans' last four games while playing through ankle and knee injuries. He can be an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield when at full strength while spelling starter Tony Pollard, but Spears hasn't provided much production while banged up. Another quiet performance from Spears is likely forthcoming in Week 7 against a Browns defense that has allowed just one TD to running backs all season, so he isn't a recommended fantasy play, even in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyjae Spears has been banged up for most of the season. He sat out Tennessee's Week 7 loss to the Browns due to a knee injury after previously playing through ankle and knee injuries. He's a shifty change-of-pace option when healthy, but Spears won't be an advisable Week 8 fantasy play even if he suits up against the Bengals. Tony Pollard has strengthened his hold on the top spot on Tennessee's RB depth chart with strong play in recent weeks, and Spears is unlikely to score his first TD of the season against a Bengals defense that has allowed just three TDs to RBs through six games.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Purdy and the 49ers will look to remain perfect with a Week 6 win over Washington. Purdy was sacked for the first time this season and threw his first pickoff since Week 1 this past Sunday against Seattle, but he also threw two touchdowns to help guide San Francisco to victory. He was especially synched up with veteran wideout Mike Evans, with whom he connected seven times for 113 yards and a score. Purdy could feast on a Commanders defense that has given up 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most in the NFL) and 27.9 fantasy points per game (second-most in the league) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Purdy and the 49ers travel to take on the Falcons in Week 7. He completed 21 of 29 pass attempts for 264 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Purdy found seven different receivers as the 49ers improved to 6-0 on the season, but it sounds like they could be without Mike Evans (Achilles) for an extended period of time. Purdy will take aim at Atlanta's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.6) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches on offense to be worth considering in fantasy against Denver's stout defense in Week 2. He had one target and one carry in Jacksonville's season opener, which he turned into 11 scrimmage yards across four snaps on offense while playing primarily on defense. Hunter played both wide receiver and cornerback at Colorado before being drafted second overall by the Jaguars in 2025. With WRs Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers ahead of him, the versatile Hunter is currently more useful to the Jaguars on defense, much to the chagrin of his fantasy managers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense in either of Jacksonville's last two games heading into a Week 4 trip to Cincinnati. The 2025 second overall pick has been playing almost exclusively on defense, so Hunter's off the fantasy radar in formats that don't count individual defensive statistics. He's trending up as a cornerback after intercepting Drake Maye in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots.
outlooksByWeek.5: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense for the Jaguars since Week 1. He played every defensive snap in Week 4 and is focusing primarily on playing cornerback rather than wide receiver. Hunter is a fantasy non-factor except in formats that reward his defensive contributions. Jacksonville will face the Eagles in Week 5 in London, where Hunter showcased his upside on offense last season with eight catches for 101 yards and a TD against the Rams. Don't expect a repeat performance anytime soon, if ever.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Hunter got his first offensive touch since Week 1 during the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Eagles, but he's being used as a full-time defensive player while barely seeing the field on offense. Barring a rash of injuries at wide receiver, the Jaguars will likely remain content using Hunter primarily at cornerback. He has enough talent to warrant a bench stash if you have space on the roster, but he isn't an appealing fantasy option in Week 6 against the Texans unless your league counts defensive contributions.
outlooksByWeek.8: Travis Hunter had his best offensive performance of the season in Week 6 against the Texans prior to Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, catching all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown. He remains a full-time defensive player, but Hunter's offensive opportunities have increased in recent weeks. The former two-way college football star tied his season high with six snaps on offense in Week 5 against the Eagles before setting a new high with nine snaps against Houston in Week 6. Hunter is a risky fantasy option due to his limited opportunities, but he has the talent to make the most of his chances and is at least a viable dart throw in deeper formats in Week 8 against a Colts defense that's giving up 25.7 points per game.

player.seasonOutlook: Full-time focus on defense should unlock rewarding production from a unique talent. Not only can Hunter mirror receivers, he frequently turns his head to track the ball, leading to big plays in coverage.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 5 when Detroit travels to Arizona. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 7 as Detroit plays the Packers. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Isiah Pacheco will stay sidelined in Week 8 as the Lions take on Minnesota. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Skyy Moore should be a depth option in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Skyy Moore was unable to catch his one target, but he also did play on offense more than was expected. The fifth-year wideout should remain a secondary choice, but he could start to garner more looks given the pass-heavy offense that Green Bay has operated with. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Skyy Moore should remain a secondary option in Green Bay's passing game against the Falcons in Week 3. Moore was utilized more in Week 2 against the Jets after Jayden Reed went down with an injury, garnering three targets and bringing in two of them for six yards. The former Kansas City wideout is the top kick returner for the Packers, but his playmaking abilities make him an interesting target for Jordan Love if he gets more involved in the offense. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Skyy Moore should continue to get opportunities as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Moore recorded three catches for 31 yards on a career-high seven targets in Week 3 against the Falcons. While a pass-heavy game script definitely helped the fifth-year wideout's cause, he has seen more of an offensive role with Jayden Reed sidelined due to a neck injury. Moore will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers in the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Skyy Moore will seek to stay involved as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Moore caught another pass in Week 5 against Tampa Bay, but it went for minus-two yards. The veteran remains an asset for Green Bay on special teams, but he'll need to do more in the coming weeks to hold any value fantasy-wise. He'll face a Chicago team that's ranked top five against fantasy wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Skyy Moore holds a questionable tag ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 matchup against the Cowboys. Moore suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter of the Packers' Week 5 blowout win over the Bears, and he was unable to return. The utility player has seen more usage with Jayden Reed out for the season with a neck injury, but he'll need to stay healthy himself if he hopes to capitalize. Moore, who has a 7-35-0 receiving line, will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Skyy Moore will remain out as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next three weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen and J. Michael Sturdivant busy on the return fronts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Skyy Moore will remain sidelined as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next  two weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton busy on the return fronts.

outlooksByWeek.2: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more effective as the Packers play the Jets in Week 2. While Lloyd was the leading rusher for Green Bay in Week 1, he still only totaled 37 yards on 13 rushing attempts. Fellow ball carrier Chris Brooks also recorded seven carries for 29 yards, so the margin between the two doesn't appear to be too large. Lloyd will look to do more with his opportunities against a New York front that should be less menacing than Minnesota's.
outlooksByWeek.3: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just 3.0 YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of its RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a top-10 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.
outlooksByWeek.4: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to turn things around as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Lloyd continued his disappointing season against the Falcons in Week 3, rushing four times for 11 yards and catching two of three passes for seven yards. While the inexperienced running back was hindered by a pass-heavy game script, he's still averaged just three yards per carry across 23 attempts and seen his offensive snap share decrease in each of his first three games. He'll also face a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs this year, making him a very risky play.
outlooksByWeek.5: MarShawn Lloyd remains in the mix of Green Bay's backfield ahead of Week 5 against Chicago. Lloyd remained extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 4, rushing the ball seven times for 13 yards, but he did salvage his performance with five catches for 36 yards. The second-year running back looks to be in direct competition with Kaleb Johnson for carries as of late, but the Packers have utilized Lloyd in different ways even when Johnson has been more effective. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.73) to RBs this season, which could give Lloyd the opening he needs to do more as a rusher.
outlooksByWeek.6: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be Green Bay's primary option in the running game again versus the Cowboys in Week 6. Lloyd put together his best fantasy performance of the year versus the Bears in Week 5, recording 10 carries for 31 yards and two touchdowns along with one catch for six yards. The second-year ball carrier has totaled 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 40 carries and caught 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score across the first five games of the campaign. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: MarShawn Lloyd could be in line for a smaller role as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Lloyd was extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 6 against the Cowboys, rushing eight times for 10 yards and logging three fewer carries than position mate Pierre Strong. Lloyd is also now set to share the backfield with a reinstated Josh Jacobs, which could further limit his opportunities. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be a complementary option once again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Lloyd's role wasn't completely chalked with the return of Josh Jacobs in Week 7, as he still logged six carries for 20 yards and caught two passes for 15 yards. Jacobs also averaged just 3.27 yards per carry on the ground, which could keep Lloyd relevant as a secondary rushing option if this persists. Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this season, so Lloyd will aim to take advantage of what could be limited touches.

player.seasonOutlook: Due to a variety of injuries, Lloyd has appeared in one game since being selected in the third round of the 2024 draft. Now healthy, he appears to have a hold on No. 2 RB duties in Green Bay, which is notable with Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. Lloyd is likely to open the season on the RB2/flex radar and should be on your radar in the middle rounds, though note that he'll fade back to no more than an insurance stash once Jacobs returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the Jaguars in Week 4. The rookie receiver caught three of five targets for 29 yards during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss, stepping up with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) out due to injuries. Meyers tied Mike Gesicki for third on the team in receptions, though he garnered two more targets than the tight end. He's still firmly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the passing game, but he's showing signs of being a reliable option in a banged-up WR room. Meyers will look to contribute against Jacksonville, whose defense ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed (527) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals visit the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He caught both of his targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both healthy, Meyers returned to a supporting role, supplying 91 yards on three kick returns and another 13 yards on two punt returns. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) could also return from a two-game absence, so both receivers could struggle to make much of a contribution against the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are at home in Week 8 to square off against Tennessee. He failed to catch either of his two targets in Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Meyers was unable to take advantage of Joe Burrow's productive day, as he threw for 292 yards and four TDs. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying a massive target share despite a solid matchup versus the Titans.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. With both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks sidelined due to injury, Lemon snagged seven passes for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He was targeted eight times in the contest. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Lemon could have a delicious matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: T.J. Hockenson remains a top option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 8 against the Lions. Hockenson found the end zone for the second time of the season in a Week 7 win over the Colts, and he complemented his score with four catches for 35 yards. The veteran tight end has now brought in 27 catches for 237 yards and two touchdowns this season. He enters a favorable matchup versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 32nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Shough will look to stay hot in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Shough was very productive in the Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for just 176 total yards but scoring four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing). Despite attempting just 30 passes in last week's win, Shough is still averaging the third-most pass attempts per game in the NFL (39.2) through six weeks. Shough could struggle against a tough Steelers defense in Week 7, as they have allowed just 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.3: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big performance when Seattle faces Washington in Week 3. With Jadarian Price suffering a shoulder injury against Arizona on Sunday, Wilson stepped up and led the Seahawks with 21 rushes for 92 yards. Price's injury isn't considered serious, but it's not certain that he'll be able to return to action in Week 3. Whoever leads Seattle's backfield will be looking to score the first rushing touchdown against the Commanders this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emanuel Wilson may be moving into a timeshare at running back for Seattle heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. An early fumble by rookie Jadarian Price was partly responsible for Wilson leading the Seahawks with nine carries in a Week 3 win over Washington, with Price logging just five totes and George Holani three. With that said, Wilson managed a paltry 14 yards on his carries, so he didn't exactly make a loud statement in a bid for more work. The Chargers just gave up 154 rushing yards to Buffalo's James Cook in Week 3, so they could be vulnerable on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big Week 4 performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Wilson led his team's backfield this past Sunday against the Chargers, posting a 21-81-1 line on the ground. Equally promising was his 3-39-1 line as a pass catcher after he logged zero receptions over the first three weeks of the campaign. With Jadarian Price (chest) on IR, Wilson figures to continue to work as Seattle's No. 1 RB, though the eventual return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) could shake up the backfield. Charbonnet isn't expected to be ready for Week 5, however, so Wilson will likely get plenty of work against the 49ers, who are middle-of-the-pack so far in giving up 17.4 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emanuel Wilson will look to get into the end zone for a third straight game when the Seahawks travel to Denver in Week 6. Wilson has emerged as Seattle's clear top RB over the past two weeks, registering 41 carries for 142 yards and two touchdowns on the ground along with five catches for 50 yards and another score through the air in that span. He figures to continue working as the team's No. 1 RB at least until one or both of Zach Charbonnet (knee) or Jadarian Price (chest) is able to return, but that won't happen in Week 6. The Broncos have been vulnerable against the run this season, surrendering 4.51 yards per carry to running backs (eighth-worst in the league).
outlooksByWeek.7: Emanuel Wilson and the Seahawks play host to the Chiefs for a Week 7 clash on Sunday Night Football. He had 14 carries for 52 yards and failed to catch his only target during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. It was an underwhelming performance for Wilson, who had scored three touchdowns over his previous two outings. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) practicing and likely to make his 2026 season debut in Week 7, it's probably best to avoid the Seahawks backfield versus Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emanuel Wilson's role for Week 8 against the Bears could depend on whether Zach Charbonnet (knee) and/or Jadarian Price (chest) is ready to rejoin Seattle's backfield. As the Seahawks' lead RB in Week 7 against Kansas City, Wilson racked up 100 yards and a touchdown on a hearty 24 carries and added one catch for 15 yards. It was the third time over his past four contests that Wilson logged 20 or more totes, but should Charbonnet and/or Price be ready to return to the fold, Wilson will likely handle a reduced workload. Either way, he could find room to run against a Chicago defense that ranks 25th in the league with 4.33 yards per carry allowed to running backs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Wan'Dale Robinson mustered just seven yards on four catches in the Titans' Week 7 loss to the Browns, and he's likely to continue earning a steady diet of short passes from Cam Ward in Week 8 against the Bengals. Robinson has 23 catches over the past five games but is averaging a career-low 7.1 yards per reception in his fifth NFL season and first with Tennessee. He's a high-floor, low-ceiling flex option for Week 8 against the Bengals, who are allowing 138 yards per game to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets.
