Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.
outlooksByWeek.8: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Mayer's volume took a significant step backward in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After turning 10 targets into an 8-82-0 line in Week 4, Mayer got only one look from Kirk Cousins in New England, turning it into a two-yard gain. Brock Bowers is the unquestioned top option in the team's passing game, but a lack of established wide receivers has created an opening for Mayer to be more than just injury insurance. Through five games, he's delivered a 21-171-1 line on 25 targets, putting him on pace for career-best numbers in 2026. Mayer will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Mayer took advantage of the extra defensive attention the Bills paid to Brock Bowers in Week 6, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 95 yards. While Bowers remains the top option in the Raiders' passing attack, Mayer is on pace for a career-best year of his own, producing a 28-266-1 line on 34 targets through six games. He is eight receptions and 63 yards away from establishing new personal bests. Mayer will likely struggle to reach those marks in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets' offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 tilt against the Bears. Despite the absence of Adonai Mitchell in Week 3, Williams logged only two targets in a game where the Jets threw 37 times. While the Bears are allowing 8.5 yards per target to receivers, Williams doesn't seem likely to garner enough looks to exploit a potentially favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Williams continues to amass minimal volume for the Jets as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Williams flashed in Week 4, finishing with 73 yards and a touchdown, but it came on just three targets. While Cleveland has allowed three receivers to top 70 yards over the last two weeks, Williams' lack of opportunities makes for a boom-or-bust play in Week 5, and that assumes Adonai Mitchell doesn't return from a two-week absence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets offense may be declining ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Despite Adonai Mitchell's three-week absence, Williams has not logged more than three targets, and his snap share fell to a season-low 59% in Week 5 with the return of Tim Patrick. The Jets aren't throwing the ball enough to sustain secondary pass-catching options, and New England is allowing just 7.5 yards per target, the ninth-lowest in the league, leaving Williams with minimal appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Young has performed very well to start the season, leading the NFL in passing yards per game (317) while accounting for 10 total touchdowns. In his most recent performance, a Week 4 win over the Lions, Young threw for a whopping 329 yards and two touchdowns. He's expected to remain one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while facing an Eagles defense that's allowed 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bryce Young is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Through five games this season, Young has thrown for 1,549 yards and accounted for 12 touchdowns with just two interceptions, leading the league with 309.8 passing yards per game. He's emerged as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while leading the Panthers' offense to 29.2 points per game, the fourth-best mark in the NFL. Expect Young to remain productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Young underwhelmed for the first time all season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, completing 14 of 27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Despite this, Young has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for an average of 285.3 yards and 2.0 touchdowns per game. He'll look to rebound in Week 8 against a strong Packers defense that's given up just 17.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacoby Brissett will aim to clean up his mistakes when Arizona hosts Detroit in Week 5. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants in Week 4 after getting picked off just once through his first three games of the season. The veteran quarterback has still been pretty productive with 818 passing yards, six touchdowns and 43 rushing yards (with one touchdown) overall this season. He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his first three-TD performance of the campaign heading into Arizona's Week 6 clash against the Rams. Two of Brissett's scores in this past Sunday's blowout loss to Detroit came after the outcome was already decided, but they count the same in the world of fantasy football. The veteran quarterbacks also threw for a season-high 292 yards and rushed for a season-best 19 yards, though he did throw his fifth interception of the campaign. Brissett could find the sledding tougher against the Rams, who have given up just 5.65 yards per attempt this season, second-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jacoby Brissett will look to build on Arizona's Week 6 victory over the Rams when the Cardinals host the Broncos in Week 7. The veteran quarterback has completed 156 of 234 passes for 1,328 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions through six games, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest. However, his 5.7 yards per attempt are the best example of the struggles Arizona's offense endures to generate explosive passing plays, and Denver represents another challenging opponent. The Broncos have allowed just 14.9 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the 12th-best mark in the NFL, limiting Brissett's appeal despite his established passing volume. He's best viewed as a lower-end QB2 in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jacoby Brissett will look to guide Arizona to more scoring in Week 8 versus Dallas. Though Brissett has thrown for a combined 490 yards over his past two games, he's tossed just one touchdown during that span. The veteran QB has taken to the air a league-high 282 times this season, so his fantasy managers have at least been able to count on consistent volume. Brissett could put up big numbers versus a Cowboys defense that ranks in the the bottom 10 of the league in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.5: Kimani Vidal is coming off his most productive game of 2026, taking five carries for 25 yards and turning three targets into a 2-11-1 line during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. While the seven touches represented a season high for Vidal, they still trailed Keaton Mitchell's 15 and Omarion Hampton's 11. Mitchell led the trio with 63 scrimmage yards, while Hampton scored a rushing TD. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is drifting toward a full-blown committee as he searches for a spark, but it would likely take an injury ahead of him for Vidal to gain significant volume on a consistent basis. He'll try to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kimani Vidal posted a season-high nine touches in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, turning eight carries into 57 yards and his first rushing touchdown of the season while also catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. The third-year back has gotten into the end zone in back-to-back games, but Vidal remains firmly in a committee with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, and none of the three would seem to have a significant ceiling while working behind a patchwork offensive line. Vidal will try to keep his TD streak going in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kimani Vidal was seeing his usage increase prior to the Chargers' Week 7 bye, with the third-year running back handling a season-high 10 touches in a Week 6 loss to Kansas City, although he turned that volume into just 40 scrimmage yards and zero TDs. Omarion Hampton remains the back with the biggest upside on the roster, but Vidal and Keaton Mitchell are also in the mix, and Mike McDaniel may deploy a full-blown committee in his backfield as he searches for answers. Vidal will face a Rams defense in Week 8 that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Returning for his third year with the Chargers, Vidal is set to compete with newcomer Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Vidal had some big moments in 2025, clearing 17 fantasy points in four games, but the notable disclaimer here is that Hampton was sidelined for all of those outings. In fact, Vidal scored only 4.1 fantasy PPG in his other nine games. The 2024 sixth-round pick is a fine depth player who showed he can handle big workloads when needed, but he'll be worth rostering only should Hampton miss time and, even then, Mitchell figures to play a role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to look like an unstoppable force for Seattle with a Week 8 matchup against the Bears on tap. Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City this past Sunday, marking his sixth performance of 100-plus receiving yards through seven weeks. The budding superstar leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns through seven weeks. He'll next face a Chicago defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 9.51 yards per target yielded to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Hubbard had his worst performance of the season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, accumulating just 60 yards on 11 touches. Across six contests this season, Hubbard has amassed 459 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six total touchdown, the 19th-most total yards in the NFL. He'll have a good opportunity to rebound in Week 8 against a Packers defense that's allowed 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.
outlooksByWeek.5: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.6: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Carnell Tate had 70 receiving yards and his first NFL touchdown in Tennessee's Week 6 win over the Colts and broke out for 145 receiving yards against the Ravens in Week 4, but he was held to just six yards by the Texans in between. The rookie, fourth overall pick is still searching for consistency in a Titans passing game that ranks among the league's worst, but Tate has shown enough upside to warrant a lineup spot as a flex option in most formats heading into a Week 7 home game against the Browns. Cleveland has been weaker than league average at defending wide receivers, allowing 157 yards per game and seven TDs in six games to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Carnell Tate has recorded at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four games, establishing himself as a reliable fantasy option despite the ongoing struggles of Titans QB Cam Ward. Facing a Bengals defense that just allowed eight catches for 137 yards and a TD to top Ravens WR Zay Flowers, Tate is a high-end flex option for Week 8. The rookie fourth overall pick is averaging more than seven targets per game and could get plenty of opportunities if the 1-6 Titans fall behind as expected on the road against the 4-2 Bengals.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed will look to make more of his opportunities as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Reed is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Packers take on the Falcons. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he hasn't seen the field since. The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Reed will not play in Week 5 as the Packers play the Bears. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jayden Reed will be inactive again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Rodriguez has a consistent role as the Jaguars' No. 2 RB behind Bhayshul Tuten, but Rodriguez's usage level is too low to warrant lineup consideration in most formats. Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first four games with the Jaguars. He's riding a two-game TD streak but has been a complete non-factor in the passing game with zero targets while averaging a mediocre 4.2 yards per carry. Jacksonville faces an Eagles defense in Week 5 that ranks among the 10 most generous to RBs on the ground, allowing 106 rushing yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Rodriguez has exceeded six rushing attempts in only one of five games with the Jaguars and has just one catch all season. With starting RB Bhayshul Tuten healthy heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans, Rodriguez doesn't look like a usable fantasy option in most formats against a stout Houston front seven that's limiting RBs to 3.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez remains a viable bench stash for managers hedging against a Tuten injury.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Rodriguez remains No. 2 on Jacksonville's RB depth chart behind Bhayshul Tuten, limiting Rodriguez's Week 8 fantasy appeal to deeper formats. Rodriguez logged a season-high 11 carries in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. He has handled fewer than six carries only once all season, but Rodriguez is a non-factor in the passing game, with just one catch in 2026. Rodriguez will be a touchdown-dependent fantasy play in Week 8 against a Colts defense that has allowed five rushing scores to RBs through seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road for an interconference clash against the Titans in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 6. Boston tied for last in receptions but finished second in targets, as Deshaun Watson completed only 16 of his 26 pass attempts. It's still a positive sign that the Browns want to get the ball in the rookie's hands despite the meager offensive output. Boston will aim to bounce back versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brenton Strange has picked up the pace after a slow start and is a viable Week 8 starter at TE for Jacksonville's home game against the Colts. He has caught 19 of 23 targets for 207 yards over the past three games after being limited to seven catches for 72 yards on 10 targets through Week 3, though Strange hasn't scored since the season opener. Strange has a nice opportunity to snap his five-game touchdown drought against the Colts, who have allowed five TDs to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam Darnold suffered a soft-tissue glute injury in Seattle's season-opening win and isn't likely to play in Week 2 against Arizona. As a result, Drew Lock is in line to guide the Seahawks' offense. Darnold isn't expected to miss significant time and could be back as soon as Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam Darnold has a chance to return from a glute injury for Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. It remains to be seen if the veteran QB will be able to suit up, but he reportedly has been ahead of schedule in his recovery. With Darnold out against Arizona in Week 2, Drew Lock took over and led the Seahawks to a win. Whichever signal-caller starts under center in Week 3 could feast upon a Washington defense that has allowed a 137.0 passer rating this season, the worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam Darnold seems to be past the glute injury that cost him some early-season action heading into Seattle's Week 4 tilt against the Chargers. Darnold returned from a one-week absence to throw for 379 yards and four touchdowns (albeit with two interceptions) in a Week 3 win against Washington. The veteran QB continued to look often to star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who logged a massive 10-128-2 receiving line on 14 targets. The Chargers have given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, 11th-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Darnold will look to lead Seattle to victory in a key NFC West clash versus San Francisco in Week 5. Darnold threw for a modest 168 yards and was picked off once against the Chargers in Week 4, but he tossed two touchdowns and guided his team to a win. After playing only five snaps over the first two weeks due to a glute injury, Darnold looks to be back to full health and has posted a 6:3 TD:INT over the Seahawks' past two games. He could face a stiff challenge against the 49ers, who have yielded only three passing TDs through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Sam Darnold will look to bounce back from a rough performance when Seattle visits Denver in Week 6. Darnold was picked off twice this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, and he threw for a modest 195 yards with one touchdown. He now has an uninspiring 7:5 TD:INT through four games after recording the third-most pickoffs (14) among NFL quarterbacks during the regular season last year. The Broncos don't figure to offer much relief, as they've yielded the fifth-best passer rating (79.4) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam Darnold and the Seahawks host the Chiefs for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He completed 27 of 51 pass attempts for 278 yards with no TDs and two INTs while rushing twice for 19 yards. Darnold has now thrown four interceptions over his last two outings while taking five sacks in each, giving him seven INTs in five games this season. It could be another rough night for Darnold in Week 7 against Kansas City's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Sam Darnold has thrown at least one pickoff in five straight games heading into Seattle's matchup against Chicago in Week 8. Darnold's eight total pickoffs are tied for most in the league despite the fact that he played only five snaps Week 1 and missed Week 2 altogether. The veteran quarterback hasn't recently been offsetting the interceptions with scores -- over his past three games, he's tossed just two total touchdowns. The Bears have given up 11 passing TDs this season, tied for eighth-most in the league, and have picked off just four passes, so perhaps Darnold can begin a turnaround.

player.seasonOutlook: Darnold's first season with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks couldn't have gone much better from a real-life standpoint, but it simply didn't translate to much fantasy success. Despite finishing fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second season in a row, Darnold finished 27th in fantasy points per game. He was very boom or bust, delivering seven top-10 weeks but also nine finishes outside the top 20. Turnovers (15 INTs were second most in the NFL) and a lack of rushing were the culprits. The 29-year-old will have a new playcaller in Brian Fleury, but otherwise it's roughly the status quo offensively. Darnold is no more than a fringe QB2 with a limited ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.
