He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return. Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Penix (ribs) will lead the Falcons' passing attack if active during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Penix was productive for the third consecutive game before exiting with a rib injury in the overtime loss to the Ravens, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. Through three weeks, Penix is averaging 239.7 passing yards and a touchdown per game. He's in for a favorable matchup if ready for Week 6, as the Bears' defense just allowed Jordan Love to throw for 367 yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense during the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Penix was productive despite a loss in Week 6, throwing for 225 yards and three touchdowns while also completing two two-point conversions. Since returning from injury, Penix has led the Falcons' offense to 31.5 points per game, the second-most in the NFL during that span. However, he could struggle against a tough 49ers defense that's given up just 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through five contests.
outlooksByWeek.8: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Penix has rejuvenated Atlanta's offense since his return from injury, throwing for an average of 231.4 yards and 1.8 touchdowns per game. He has thrown for three touchdowns in consecutive games while turning the ball over just once, leading the Falcons to 30 points per game during that span. Despite this, Penix is in for a tough Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 18.5 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonah Coleman had the biggest share of the backfield workload in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, handling 11 touches to J.K. Dobbins' six and RJ Harvey's five. Coleman's 69 scrimmage yards led the trio, but the other two each made trips to the end zone while the rookie RB was held out. It was still an impressive effort in his return from an IR stint due to an ankle injury, and Coleman might be the most likely player from the group to emerge as the lead back. A messy committee is the more probable arrangement, however, heading into a Week 8 clash with a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.3: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson is a potential breakout candidate in his second NFL season. As expected, the 2025 second-rounder played a situational role behind the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen as a rookie. He didn't get much run, but when he did, he was used as a vertical threat to the extreme. His 17.5 aDOT is highest by any tight end (minimum 10 targets) in at least a decade. The Rams are returning the same tight end room plus second-round pick Max Klare, so while consistent production could prove elusive, Ferguson very well could emerge as the No. 3 pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and 33-year-old Davante Adams in the Rams' elite offense. The 23-year-old, who also saw five end zone targets as a rookie, is worth a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Antonio Williams should see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Williams has double-digit catches in every game thus far during his rookie year, and should slot in just behind Stefon Diggs in terms of opportunities in the passing game moving forward. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.
outlooksByWeek.4: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.
outlooksByWeek.5: James Cook will likely require volume to exploit a Rams defense when the Bills face them in their Week 5 Monday night affair. Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.
outlooksByWeek.6: James Cook will seek the end zone for the fifth straight week when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. While Cook hasn't been heavily targeted in the passing game, he's posted 100-plus yard rushing efforts in three of his last four outings, garnering at least 21 carries at the same rate. Buffalo is a run-first offense, and the Week 6 matchup is very appealing; Las Vegas allows 5.2 yards per carry, again setting up Cook to be a top-tier option.
outlooksByWeek.8: James Cook needs heavy volume in Week 8 to bolster Buffalo's offense against the Ravens. That hasn't been a problem, as he's amassed 20-plus touches in four of the Bills' first six outings, and he's continued scoring, finding the end zone in each of his last five games. Prior to a Week 7 bye, Cook had his best game as a receiver, possibly elevating his floor even higher. Baltimore is a stout defense against the run, allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, the eighth-lowest total in the league, but they have surrendered 86 yards or more to an opposing back three times. Barring an unexpected change in usage, Cook should be able to flirt with those numbers in Week 8.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are on the road to take on Miami's third-ranked defense against wide receivers in Week 5. He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tee Higgins and the Bengals travel to Baltimore for a divisional clash in Week 7. He caught two of four targets for 22 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Higgins was able to battle through an adductor injury that kept him limited in practices leading up to the contest, and he has now had a bye week for some added rest. He draws a favorable matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 34.1 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 22nd.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an AFC showdown against the Titans in Week 8. He caught six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. Higgins tied with Ja'Marr Chase (5-62-1) in targets but paced the Bengals in receptions and yardage for the second time in three contests. Higgins will aim to keep rolling against a Titans defense allowing 35.8 fantasy points per game to WRs, which is tied for 24th.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tucker Kraft will look to do more with his targets as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Kraft stayed involved in Week 6 against the Cowboys, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has continued to get opportunities with a 25-249-1 receiving line off 37 targets, but he still sits behind the two-man punch of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson at this point in the year. Luckily for Kraft, the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (31.9) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quentin Johnston wasn't able to get much going in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards. The entire passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel wasn't yet in rhythm aside from Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey isn't able to play in Week 2, Johnston could be the biggest beneficiary when it comes to additional volume from Justin Herbert. Johnston will face a Raiders secondary in Week 2 that was tied for 21st in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quentin Johnston has struggled through the Chargers' first two games, catching just three of 11 targets for 24 yards. The fourth-year wideout had emerged as a deep option over the prior two seasons, but new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme is built on quick passes and yards after the catch, giving little time for Johnston's typical downfield routes to develop. Tre' Harris and rookie speedster Brenan Thompson both seem better suited to that style of passing game, and Johnston runs a real risk of becoming an afterthought as the season progresses. He does at least get a potentially favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quentin Johnston could be in danger of losing his spot as the Chargers' No. 2 wide receiver. The 2023 first-round pick leads the team with 17 targets through three games, but that volume has resulted in just a 6-64-0 line, and Johnston has been unable to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's limitations due to a rib injury. Second-year WR Tre' Harris did in Week 3, suggesting he could be about to move past Johnston in the pecking order. Johnston will have a hard time building any momentum in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quentin Johnston saw only two targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but he was able to turn one of them into a 44-yard gain for his only catch. The season-low volume was especially disappointing given that Ladd McConkey left the game early with a foot injury. The passing game as a whole is struggling, and Johnston could end up getting passed on the depth chart by Tre' Harris if he doesn't begin to make a more consistent impact. Johnston will try to earn more look from Justin Herbert in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quentin Johnston was unable to play through a chest injury in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, missing his first game of the season. The fourth-year wideout has just a 7-108-0 line on 19 targets in four contests, and the team's offensive struggles under coordinator Mike McDaniel have dragged down essentially every skill player on the roster. If Johnston returns in Week 6, it will be for a brutal matchup against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quentin Johnston has struggled this season along with the rest of the Chargers' offense, catching only one pass in three of his five games and failing to reach 60 receiving yards or score a TD in any of them. He has had receptions of 40-plus yards in each of his last two contests, however, reaffirming that he does have some big-play upside. Johnston faces a tough test in Week 8 against a Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Four weeks into the 2025 season, it appeared Johnston was on the verge of a breakout campaign. The 2023 first-round pick found the end zone four times and scored 14-plus fantasy points in each game during the span. The return to earth was abrupt, as Johnston went on to average 9.2 PPG in his final 10 games. The 25-year-old has posted consistent receiving lines in each of the last two seasons (55-724-8 and 51-735-8), but neither resulted in a top-30 fantasy campaign. The Chargers offense should be better in 2026 with a healthy line and Mike McDaniel calling plays, but Johnston is unlikely to see a big boost in usage with the likes of Ladd McConkey and sophomores Tre Harris and Omarion Hampton also in the fold. Johnston is no more than a boom/bust flex in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tre Tucker continues to build chemistry with Kirk Cousins. The Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver hauled in two touchdowns in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, and through six games Tucker has produced a 24-371-3 line on 35 targets, putting him on pace for his first 1,000-yard effort. Tight end Brock Bowers remains the top option in the passing game, and Tucker has yet to record more than eight targets in a game in 2026. The prospect of Fernando Mendoza replacing Cousins under center at some point offers additional uncertainty for Tucker. He'll have a hard time delivering another ceiling game in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tre Tucker is on his way to a career-best season with Kirk Cousins under center for the Raiders. The fourth-year wideout has caught 10 of 19 targets for 200 yards and three touchdowns over the last two games, and through seven contests Tucker sports a 29-474-4 line on 47 targets. Brock Bowers is still the team's top downfield threat, but Tucker is establishing himself as a strong No. 2 option, although the eventual switch at QB to rookie Fernando Mendoza could change things. Tucker will look to keep rolling in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre' Harris wasn't able to take advantage of the absences of Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He played 30 snaps, catching two of four targets for 16 yards before also getting hurt. Harris is viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but he was already struggling to make an impression in a Mike McDaniel scheme that is performing well below expectations in all areas. If Harris does get cleared to play in Week 6, he'll be facing a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tre' Harris missed the Chargers' last game before a bye due to a hamstring injury, but the time off could allow him to return to the lineup. The bigger issue for the second-year wideout is the state of the offense around him, as he's topped 60 receiving yards only once in five games and is still looking for his first touchdown of 2026. Ladd McConkey could also return from an injury in Week 8, which might leave Harris struggling to get significant volume against a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emmett Johnson continues to work his way into the Kansas City game plan as a pass-catcher. Over the last two games, the rookie has corralled four of six targets for 35 yards while the team deals with injuries to its wide receiver corps. Johnson will not challenge a healthy Kenneth Walker as the lead back, but Andy Reid is trying to find ways to get Johnson the ball in space. The result has been a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through his first six NFL games. Johnson will look to score his first career touchdown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing six times for 40 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Watson was sacked eight times for 53 yards and fumbled three times, although he recovered two of them. After leading the Browns to a three-game win streak behind strong performances, Watson struggled with pressure and the rainy conditions in the Week 5 defeat. He'll aim to bounce back versus Baltimore's 12th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to square off against the Titans in Week 7. He completed 16 of 26 pass attempts for 164 yards and rushed eight times for 29 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. Watson is not much of a fantasy-friendly quarterback, but he has the Browns at 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Next up is a stingy Tennessee defense that ranks 10th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a divisional clash in Week 8. He completed 25 of 36 pass attempts for 308 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while rushing three times for 19 yards and a TD during Cleveland's Week 7 victory. Watson mounted a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter for the fifth time this season, leading the Browns to a 5-2 record and a tie with the Steelers atop the AFC North. He'll face Pittsburgh's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.1) to QBs for the second time in 2026. Watson threw for 268 yards with one TD and one INT to go along with 22 rush yards in a Week 4 win over the Steelers.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench.
