outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Harrison could make his Texans debut in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Harrison will likely be brought along slowly after being acquired in a trade from Arizona, so expectations should be tempered for Week 6, though the 2024 fourth overall pick is at least worth a flier in deeper leagues against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers. Harrison had just 85 receiving yards in four games for the Cardinals this season, but a reunion with former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud could be what Harrison needs to get his career back on track. While catching passes from Stroud in 2022, Harrison posted his best college season, with 77 catches for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Harrison was on the field for only 12 snaps in his Texans debut against the Jaguars in Week 6 but came away with three catches for 34 yards from former college teammate C.J. Stroud. Harrison's role figures to grow as he gets acclimated to his new surroundings and learns the playbook. The trade acquisition from Arizona had only 85 receiving yards through four games with the Cardinals this season, but Harrison was considered an elite wide receiver prospect when he was drafted fourth overall in 2024. He's certainly worth a speculative add if available, but Harrison will remain a risky flex option in Week 7 against the Giants since his usage is likely to be limited again.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. He amassed 13 carries in Week 4, one fewer than TreVeyon Henderson's 14, but Stevenson found the end zone while catching three passes for the third time in four weeks. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rhamondre Stevenson could garner workhorse carries in the Patriots' Week 6 match against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an ankle issue. Stevenson had 13 carries in Week 5 for the second straight week and now has double-digit carries in three of five games while adding at least three catches four times. With double-digit touches seemingly certain, Stevenson can exploit a defense that's allowing 4.3 yards per carry and one where he posted 102 yards and two touchdowns on only 13 touches last season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't had much room to run for the Patriots in advance of a Week 7 clash with the Bears. Stevenson has logged double-digit carries in four of his first six games but is averaging a career-low 3.7 yards per carry while sharing time with TreVeyon Henderson, who surprisingly played in Week 6 despite a high-ankle sprain. Chicago has allowed only three rushing scores, and no opposing runner has topped 61 yards since Week 3, so while volume will remain Stevenson's friend, he'll likely need to find the end zone to provide fair returns.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots' passing game will keep him active in Week 8 against the Dolphins. While he is coming off his third single-digit carry game of the season, he's caught at least three passes in five games and five in two outings, an area where Miami's defense is particularly vulnerable. The Dolphins allow a moderate 4.3 yards per carry and just three rushing touchdowns to backs, yet have given up 34 catches, including five touchdown receptions, to running backs in six games. Stevenson has multiple paths to meaningful production.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game. He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Addison will aim to do more with his targets as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Addison didn't do much again in Week 7 against the Colts, reeling in two of his three targets for 30 yards. The speedy pass catcher has put together an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, totaling just 13 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown across five games. He'll look to capitalize on a faulty Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Ferguson had a two-game scoring streak snapped for the Cowboys. Ferguson managed three catches for just 11 yards in the 34-30 win over the Texans. Ferguson has just 12 catches for 83 yards through the first four games of the season, though has scored three times over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Ferguson saw a season-high six targets last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which likely contributed to the additional looks for other players, including Ferguson. However, Ferguson managed three catches for just 19 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Ferguson back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Ferguson continues to struggle to find his place in the Dallas offense. Ferguson managed just two catches for 13 yards in the dismal 23-13 loss to the Packers. Ferguson has been held out of the end zone in three-straight games, and has failed to gain even 20 yards receiving in any of those contests. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Ferguson was held without a catch last game for Dallas. Ferguson's decline has been steep this season. He has failed to find the end zone in four-straight games, and has not even gained 20 yards in any contest over that span. He will look to get back on track in Week 8 with an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Mason could be in line for a workhorse role as the Vikings travel to Detroit in Week 8. Mason made his return from IR in Week 7 against the Colts and logged 15 carries for 68 yards, leading the ground game with Aaron Jones hurting his knee in the matchup. Jones' status is up in the air moving forward, so Mason's role could be even bigger if he has full command of the backfield. The Lions have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.
outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets. After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Schultz was second on the Texans in targets behind Nico Collins during the season opener, which matched Schultz's usage last season. After being thrown to eight times in Week 1 against a Bills defense that allowed the fewest yards in the NFL to TEs last season, Schultz is poised for a hefty Week 2 workload against a Bengals defense that surrendered the most yards to his position in 2025. Schultz's role and matchup make him a top-10 fantasy TE for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Schultz paced the Texans with 12 catches for 140 yards on 14 targets in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, working as C.J. Stroud's top target in the absence of WR Nico Collins (hamstring). The veteran TE is the favorite to lead the team in targets if Collins sits in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most yards and TDs in the NFL this season. Indianapolis just allowed nine catches for 101 yards and a TD to Chiefs TE Travis Kelce in Week 2. Schultz is locked in as a fantasy TE1 for Week 3 if Collins sits and has a strong argument to stay in that range even if Collins suits up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Schultz is coming off a disappointing 30-yard outing in Week 3 against the Colts, but he'll remain a fantasy TE1 in Week 4 against the Cowboys if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game. Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 85 receiving yards per game since Collins got hurt. The Cowboys have struggled to defend TEs, allowing three TDs while forcing only two incompletions on 19 passes to the position. If Collins returns, Schultz will maintain fantasy starter-level upside but with a lower floor due to dropping a spot in the pass-catching hierarchy.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Schultz has recorded just 39 yards in two games since his 140-yard outburst for the Texans in Week 2. He's back to working as a supporting piece in Houston's passing game now that Nico Collins has recovered from a hamstring injury. The 30-year-old TE's inconsistent workloads keep him from being a reliable fantasy starter, and Schultz will be tough to trust in Week 5 against a Titans defense that's holding his position to 27 receiving yards per game, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Schultz leads the Texans with 24 catches heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Jaguars in London, though half of those receptions came in Week 2 against the Bengals. Jacksonville has been among the five stingiest defenses against TEs, limiting the position to 3.6 catches for 34 yards per game. The Jaguars have allowed two TDs to the position, but Schultz has scored only five times in 39 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 season and is still searching for his first TD of the season. Despite Schultz's respectable target volume, he's best left on the bench in single-TE formats in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dalton Schultz has exceeded 35 receiving yards just once through Houston's first six games of the season and has yet to score a TD heading into a Week 7 home game against the Giants. He's a secondary option in a Houston passing game that has gotten more production out of its WRs in recent weeks, and Schultz's lack of red-zone involvement compared to other middling TE options makes him an unappealing fantasy play. The Giants have limited TEs to two TDs this season, so Schultz is best left on the bench or waivers since his TD drought is unlikely to end in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.6: Dameon Pierce was the last running back standing for the Eagles last game. Will Shipley started the game and found the end zone early for the Eagles, but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. Pierce could start against the Panthers, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Saquon Barkley's place last game for the Eagles.  Pierce also caught four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley cannot suit up in Week 7 due to his balky hamstring, Pierce would be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dameon Pierce still managed to maintain a solid role despite the return of Saquon Barkley from injury for the Eagles.  Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown but tweaked his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. This allowed Pierce to take 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown of his own.  However, Pierce could be seen leaving the field late in the fourth quarter with a potential injury as well. If neither Barkley nor Pierce can play in Week 8 versus Washington, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back. The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kaelon Black and the 49ers visit the Falcons for a Week 7 showdown. He had eight carries for 34 yards and caught his lone target for three yards in San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Christian McCaffrey tallied 25 touches to the rookie's nine, leaving no doubt about who the leader is in the 49ers' backfield. Black will look to make more of an impact with his limited touches versus Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.
